gen-mystery-quest-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans reads sturdy and large, its lowercase standing high and each e opening clearly to the right. And Mystery Quest, bookish and nostalgic, lets curved strokes gape with open jaws above compact ascenders.
gen-gf-grandstander-fs-public-sans: Poured-ink fun with letters held open: Grandstander keeps its line width constant, ascenders short and lowercase tall, all bold and expressive. Public Sans steps in with hefty lowercase and broad open counters.
gen-press-start-2p-fs-asap: Press Start 2P pins its letters far apart, like cut-outs. Asap, readable and sans-serif with c forms that sweep as open arcs, keeps the text moving smoothly since its lowercase height nearly matches the capitals.
gen-gf-gugi-general-sans: Gugi cuts its terminals open so the counters flow outward. Smooth curves link them: General Sans, a sans-serif with steady pressure, rounds every bend as freely as Gugi's open terminals do.
gen-gf-metamorphous-switzer: Switzer builds tubular, wire-like letters whose c tips never close. Hand-drawn ink in Metamorphous against Switzer's unshifting weight is what makes the pair stand apart, wide sidebearings and all.
gen-righteous-fs-fira-sans: Righteous bends thin steel rod into bowls that fill the line. Where Righteous grabs attention, Fira Sans does the quieter work, with s curves open at both ends, uniform stroke weight and a generous lowercase height.
gen-righteous-fs-merriweather-sans: Righteous draws like toothpaste squeezed in one steady line. Against it, Merriweather Sans stands sturdy and large, its e opening clearly to the right, a solid counterweight to the bounce.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-switzer: Switzer reads tubular and wire-like, its c tips never creeping toward touching and its bowls weighted like its stems. Snowburst One shouts in stencil bridges; Switzer keeps things approachable.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-satoshi: Tube-bold and splay-tipped, Tilt Neon commands the line. Both fonts hold their stroke width constant, but Satoshi, sans-serif and approachable, adds a towering lowercase with an e that never squeezes shut.
gen-dafont-blockletter-archivo: Pencil-sketched and precise, Blockletter never presses harder. Archivo, sans-serif and editorial, lets its curves open outward with a commanding x-height, giving that steady pencil line a much freer partner.
